questions.question: A recently excavated 2,000-year-old Buddhist site in Jammu and Kashmir belong to which historical period
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Kushan period.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] __In News__

__
 
• A 2,000-year-old Buddhist site was discovered at Zehanpora village in Baramulla district of Jammu and Kashmir, highlighting the region’s ancient Buddhist heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__

__
 
• The archaeological site at Zehanpora dates back nearly 2,000 years and is associated with the Kushan period.
 
• The excavation revealed stupas, monastic buildings, and structural remains typical of ancient Buddhist centres.
 
• Drone surveys confirmed that the mounds at Zehanpora are man-made and not natural formations.
 
• The site lies on an ancient trade and pilgrimage route linking Gandhara with Kashmir, underlining its historical importance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

__
 
• Kushan Period__

 __
 
• Flourished roughly between the 1st and 3rd centuries CE.
 
• Known for patronage of Buddhism and development of stupas and monasteries.
 
• Played a key role in linking Central Asia, Gandhara, and the Indian subcontinent through trade routes.
 
 
 
• Gandharan Influence__
 __
 
• An ancient region covering parts of present-day northwest Pakistan and eastern Afghanistan.
 
• Famous for Gandhara art, which influenced Buddhist architecture and sculpture.
 
• The layouts of stupas and monastic cells at Zehanpora resemble Gandharan designs.
 
 
 
• Huvishkapura__
 
 
• Believed to be a Kushan-era capital linked to Kashmir.
 
• Zehanpora is thought to have served as an important Buddhist centre connected to this capital.

questions.question: Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan announced the introduction of a new Seed Act to replace which outdated legislation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seeds Act, 1966.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Legislative Reform:** Union Agriculture Minister **Shivraj Singh Chouhan** announced in March 2026 that the Government of India introduced a new **Seed Act**.
 
• **Modernization:** This new legislation is designed to replace the nearly six-decade-old **Seeds Act of 1966**, which is no longer sufficient to address modern agricultural challenges and biotechnological advancements.
 
• **Objective:** The primary goal is to ensure the availability of **high-quality, certified seeds** to farmers while regulating the entry of spurious or low-quality seeds into the market.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Features of the Proposed Act__**

__
 
• **Mandatory Registration:** The new Act will likely mandate the registration of all seed varieties to maintain a national database and ensure traceability.
 
• **Quality Standards:** It aims to set higher benchmarks for **germination, genetic purity, and physical purity**.
 
• **Price Regulation:** The Act may include provisions for the government to intervene in seed pricing during emergencies or to prevent exploitation by private companies.
 
• **Farmers' Rights:** While regulating commercial trade, the Act is expected to protect the traditional rights of farmers to **save, use, sow, and exchange** farm-saved seeds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Background & Necessity__**

 
• **Technology Gap:** The 1966 Act was formulated during the Green Revolution and lacks specific provisions for **Genetically Modified (GM)** seeds and advanced hybrid technology.
 
• **Global Alignment:** The new law aims to align Indian seed regulations with international standards, facilitating easier exports and global research collaborations.
 
• **Penalty Structure:** The outdated 1966 Act has low penalties for non-compliance; the new Act proposes **stricter punishments** for the sale of misbranded or substandard seeds to safeguard farmers' livelihoods.

questions.question: Which of the following wetlands was designated as India’s 100th Ramsar site on World Environment Day, June 5, 2026?

options.text: Surha Tal (Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Surha Tal (Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**
__
• On **World Environment Day** (June 5, 2026), India designated **Surha Tal** of **Ballia, Uttar Pradesh**, as its **100th Ramsar site**.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**
__
• **Surha Tal**, also known as the **Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary**, is located in the **middle stretch of the Ganga River basin** in **Ballia**.
• It is a **freshwater wetland** originally formed from a **meander of the Ganga** and receives freshwater through three channels.
• With this designation, the wetland becomes the **world’s 2,595th Ramsar site** under the **1971 Ramsar Convention**.
• The site provides a critical refuge for waterbirds such as the vulnerable **common pochard** (Aythya ferina) and the **Indian river tern** (Sterna aurantia), especially during summer months.
• It also supports the vulnerable **fishing cat** (Prionailurus viverrinus), which uses the wetland as a feeding ground.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
__
• India now has the **highest number of Ramsar wetlands in Asia** and the **third highest in the world**, trailing only the **UK (176)** and **Mexico (144)**.
• The number of Indian Ramsar sites has increased from **26 to 100** in the past **11 years**, with **58 sites** added in the last four years alone.
• The **Ramsar Convention** was adopted in **1971** in the Iranian city of **Ramsar** and includes **172 member countries**.
** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

• The sanctuary supports a rich biodiversity including **221 plant species**, **66 fish species** (including vulnerable Wallago attu), **seven reptile species**, and **three amphibian species**.
• Management measures such as **seasonal controls** and **prohibition of destructive practices** are in place to address over-fishing and aquatic resource harvesting.

questions.question: Which two Supreme Court judges constituted the bench that took suo motu cognisance of illegal mining and the gharial habitat crisis in the Chambal region?

options.text: Justice Sanjiv Khanna and Justice Bela Trivedi
Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta
Justice B.R. Gavai and Justice Pankaj Mithal
Justice Surya Kant and Justice Dipankar Datta

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Supreme Court took suo motu cognisance of illegal mining activities along the Chambal River and the resulting threat to gharial habitats.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The bench comprised Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta.**
 
• The Court observed that uncontrolled illegal mining was damaging breeding and nesting habitats of gharials in the Chambal region.
 
• The matter involved concerns regarding an alleged attempt to exclude **732 hectares** from the National Chambal Gharial Sanctuary.
 
• The next hearing in the case was scheduled for **2 April 2026.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Chambal Gharial Sanctuary**__

 __
 
• The sanctuary is a protected area dedicated to conservation of gharials and aquatic biodiversity.
 
• It extends across Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Legal Provisions Involved**__
 __
 
• Violations were linked to the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
 
• Other relevant laws included the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 and Biological Diversity Act, 2002.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Accountability**__
 __
 
• The Supreme Court issued notices to Chief Secretaries and senior officials of Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The Court warned of possible personal accountability for administrative inaction.
 
 
 
• **Amicus Curiae**__
 
 
• Senior Advocate Nikhil Goyal and Advocate-on-Record Rupali Samuel were appointed as Amicus Curiae.
 
• An Amicus Curiae assists the court by providing legal expertise and independent advice.

questions.question: Which Union Ministry has launched the 'SAHI' and 'BODH' initiatives at India AI Impact Summit 2026?

questions.solution:

• **SAHI (Strategy for Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare for India):**

 
 
• Functions as a **national policy roadmap** and governance framework.
 
• Ensures AI integration remains **accountable, equitable, and transparent**.
 
• Guides hospitals, states, and private partners on data stewardship and ethical AI deployment.

questions.question: What is the primary focus of the GARBH-INi initiative, India's largest pregnancy cohort study recently discussed by Dr. Jitendra Singh?

questions.question: Which dignitary addressed the joint session of Parliament at the beginning of 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President Droupadi Murmu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The joint session of Parliament is addressed by the President of India at the beginning of the first session of each year, as per Article 87 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• In January 2025, President Droupadi Murmu, as the current President of India, will address the joint session of Parliament.
 
• This address outlines the government’s policies, plans, and legislative agenda for the upcoming year.
 
• The President’s speech is prepared by the government and reflects its vision and priorities.
 
• President Droupadi Murmu is the 15th President of India and the first tribal woman to hold the office, assuming the position on July 25, 2022.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar (Option 1):**

 
 
• The Vice President of India serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Upper House of Parliament).
 
• While the Vice President presides over Rajya Sabha sessions, he does not address the joint session of Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Speaker Om Birla (Option 3):**
 
 
• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha (Lower House of Parliament) presides over Lok Sabha sessions and plays a crucial role in maintaining order and ensuring the smooth conduct of business.
 
• The Speaker does not address the joint session of Parliament; their primary responsibility is to manage the proceedings of the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Prime Minister Narendra Modi (Option 4):**
 
 
• The Prime Minister is the head of the government and is responsible for the execution of policies and administration.
 
• Although the Prime Minister participates in parliamentary proceedings and debates, the address to the joint session is the constitutional duty of the President.
 
 
 
• **Address to the Joint Session of Parliament:**
 
 
• The President’s address to the joint session is a ceremonial event marking the start of the parliamentary year.
 
• This practice allows the government to present its agenda and priorities to both Houses of Parliament simultaneously.
 
• The address is followed by a debate in both Houses, where members discuss the content of the speech.

questions.question: A sessions court, as per the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha (Second) Sanhita, 2023, is mandated to frame charges within _____ days from the first hearing on such charges.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sixty days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha (Second) Sanhita, 2023, sessions courts are required to frame charges within **sixty days** from the first hearing on such charges.
 
• This provision aims to ensure timely prosecution and prevent unnecessary delays in legal proceedings.
 
• The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, seeks to replace the colonial-era Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) and modernize the judicial process in India.
 
• It focuses on transparency, accountability, and the expeditious handling of cases in order to strengthen the criminal justice system.
 
• The sixty-day timeframe underscores the importance of adhering to strict deadlines to enhance judicial efficiency and uphold justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: Fifteen days**

 
 
• Fifteen days is an insufficient time frame for framing charges in most sessions court cases, as it does not provide adequate time for legal review and preparation.
 
• This period is more commonly associated with preliminary procedures or remand orders in certain cases.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Seventy-five days**
 
 
• Although seventy-five days could allow for more detailed case preparation, it exceeds the mandated sixty-day period specified in the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
 
• Such a delay could undermine the objective of expediting the judicial process.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: One hundred and twenty days**
 
 
• This period is significantly longer than necessary for framing charges in sessions court cases.
 
• Delays of this magnitude could lead to prolonged judicial processes and deny justice to victims and accused individuals alike.
 
 
 
• **Context of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023**
 
 
• The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, is a comprehensive reform aimed at updating the criminal laws of India.
 
• It replaces outdated provisions in the CrPC to align with contemporary legal and social requirements.
 
• The reform emphasizes the protection of citizens' rights, timely delivery of justice, and reduced pendency of cases in courts.

questions.question: India set a new Guinness World Record in 2025 for the largest human formation of which of the following symbols?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka Chakra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India set a new **Guinness World Record in 2025** for the largest human formation of the **Ashoka Chakra**, a symbol of peace, dharma, and progress.
 
• The event took place with the participation of thousands of people who came together to form the intricate design of the **Ashoka Chakra**, which is featured prominently on the Indian national flag.
 
• The **Ashoka Chakra** consists of 24 spokes, representing the 24 virtues such as love, courage, patience, and righteousness, which are significant in Indian cultural and philosophical heritage.
 
• This record-breaking event was organized to promote unity, patriotism, and the values that the **Ashoka Chakra** symbolizes in Indian society.
 
• The Guinness World Record team verified the formation's accuracy and adherence to the dimensions of the **Ashoka Chakra** as depicted on the national flag.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ashoka Chakra:**

 
 
• The **Ashoka Chakra** is derived from the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath, which is one of the most prominent symbols of India's rich heritage.
 
• It represents the **wheel of dharma**, embodying the principles of truth, justice, and progress.
 
• The 24 spokes in the chakra symbolize the life cycle and virtues essential for maintaining harmony and balance.
 
• It is prominently displayed in the center of the **Indian national flag**, signifying motion and dynamism.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Guinness World Records:**
 
 
• Guinness World Records is an internationally recognized authority for documenting extraordinary feats and achievements.
 
• India has consistently set records in various domains, showcasing its cultural, social, and scientific achievements.
 
• Events like the formation of the **Ashoka Chakra** highlight the nation's unity and collective spirit.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Symbols:**
 
 
• **Heart Shape:** Globally recognized as a symbol of love and compassion.
 
• **Olympic Rings:** Representing the unity of five continents and the Olympic spirit.
 
• **Peace Symbol:** Widely used to signify harmony and the absence of conflict.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context of the Ashoka Chakra:**
 
 
• The chakra is named after **Emperor Ashoka**, one of India's greatest rulers, who embraced Buddhism and propagated values of peace and dharma.
 
• It is a reminder of India's commitment to universal values and moral principles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Guinness World Record Verification:**

 
 
• The record-breaking formation required precise planning and execution to accurately depict the **Ashoka Chakra**.
 
• Participants were trained to understand the design and significance of the symbol.
 
• Such events foster patriotism and are a celebration of India's national identity.
 
 
 
• **Role of Symbols in National Identity:**
 
 
• Symbols like the **Ashoka Chakra** play a pivotal role in expressing the ethos and values of a nation.
 
• They are used in national events, government documents, and cultural representations.
 
• Educational programs often emphasize their importance to instill respect and pride in citizens.

questions.question: According to the recent announcement by the Ministry of Education, which foreign university is set to establish its campus at **Manyata Business Park** in **Bengaluru**?

__
• The **Ministry of Education** issued **Letters of Approval (LoA)** to three globally reputed foreign higher education institutions to set up campuses in India.
• The ceremony was attended by Union Minister for Education, **Shri Dharmendra Pradhan**, where LoAs were handed over to the **University of Bristol**, **University of York**, and **University of New South Wales (UNSW)**.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

• **University of York**: This university will set up its first overseas campus in **Mumbai**, focusing on Finance, AI, Cyber Security, and Creative Industries.
• **Alignment with Innovation Hubs**: The selection of **Mumbai** and **Bengaluru** aligns with India’s most dynamic knowledge and technology hotspots, with Bengaluru being described as the **Silicon Valley of the East**.

• The **UGC Regulations** for foreign universities aim to provide a transparent, time-bound framework for establishing campuses while maintaining **institutional autonomy**.
• The move is expected to expand access to high-quality international education and strengthen research collaborations between India, the **UK**, and **Australia**.
